conclusions: Reward D replaces positive instantaneous angular-velocity shaping with signed angular displacement; it is not a simple additional bonus.
Native success coefficient600 is integrated by dt1/60, giving a one-time success reward10. Formula reconstruction matches saved data to floating point error.
Gamma0.99 is applied per60Hz physical transition, with about1.67s effective horizon; this is a design risk, not an implementation scaling mismatch.

Critic consumes unexecuted proposed residual as well as executed action. Real recorded contexts show Q changes for mathematically identical executed actions. This common modeling risk is not established as the cause of D-C performance differences.
Actor already made376/378 updates before first completed episode. Dense rewards exist, but successful terminal tails were not yet anchored.
Observed final-policy Q differs substantially from realized soft returns; correlated single continuations are not calibrated expected-Q ground truth.
Net-progress shaping reduces inflated failure returns, so reverting to positive-velocity-only shaping is not justified by this audit.
Seed0 final sampled random test D107/128 versus A109/128; multi-seed evidence remains incomplete.
